item.title: [Due in 3 days] Entra switches off unused or failing SMS first-factor sign-in tenant by tenant; the rollout now runs to the end of November 2026
item.description:
SMS first-factor sign-in skips MFA and Microsoft cites significant fraud against it; tenants that still use it can lose it for frontline users at any point until the end of November, and tenants that do not use it keep a phishable path enabled until Microsoft clears it.

Entra · deadline 2026-11-30 · Review SMS first-factor sign-ins (SignInNoPassword) for the last 30 days, give every SMS-only user another method, and clear 'Use for sign-in' yourself if nobody needs it.

item.title: [New] Two new Graph permissions read and write the Entra authentication feature toggle policy: Policy.Read.AuthFeatureToggle and Policy.ReadWrite.AuthFeatureToggle (privilege level 4)
item.description:
An app granted the ReadWrite permission can PATCH a tenant-wide authentication policy without a signed-in user; it is a new consent string that existing app-consent reviews and alert rules do not know.

Graph · Add both names to the watch list of app-consent and service-principal permission alerts, and treat any grant of Policy.ReadWrite.AuthFeatureToggle as a tier-0 change.

item.title: [New] Bring Your Own Telephony (BYOT) is now generally available beside CYOT; Microsoft-provided SMS and voice still start retiring on 1 February 2027
item.description:
The telephony integration becomes a tier-0 component in an Azure subscription: whoever can change it controls MFA code delivery, and SMS pumping fraud is billed to the tenant.

Entra · Decide which users truly need SMS or voice, move everyone else to passkeys, and if a provider is needed lock down the Azure subscription hosting the integration (RBAC, activity-log alerts) before 1 February 2027.
